scope.tested: A bounded non-destructive finite model of repository-local claim/idempotency under a FIXED destination-repository incarnation. Claim transition is a generation-scoped unique-path create. Compared permanent monotonic ownership, wall-clock lease/timeout takeover without fencing, explicit generation handoff recorded separately from the effect authority, and explicit generation handoff plus terminal effect commit serialized through the same CAS authority object.

dimensions.two_concurrent_claimers: always present; both target the same generation-scoped claim path

assumptions: Destination repository incarnation is fixed for the entire trace; Part125's same-name repository rebind problem is intentionally held orthogonal and remains unresolved.
Workers are crash/retry/concurrency faulty but not Byzantine: a worker attempts terminal effect commit only after proving that its token owns the generation-scoped claim path.

The current connected Chat GitHub create_file contract is create-only for a named path: the path must not already exist. Current update_file uses the current blob SHA as the file-level CAS precondition.

For the strong handoff policy, generation advance and terminal repository-local effect status mutate the SAME authority file by current-blob CAS. A later invocation may attempt at most one generation handoff; no wall-clock expiry or lease is used.

Liveness for abandoned claims is conditional on at least one later fair scheduled invocation obtaining a mutation opportunity. Infinite adversarial preemption or a permanent repository outage is outside the tested scope.
not_tested: Repository same-name delete/recreate or force-rebind after precheck
Byzantine workers that intentionally ignore claim ownership
External/non-repository side effects whose sink does not participate in the same generation fence
Global asynchronous liveness under infinitely many preempting invocations
Plan-entitlement or paid-plan independence beyond the already-connected lightweight repository transport surface

public_source_evidence.source: GitHub Docs, REST API endpoints for repository contents
public_source_evidence.relevant_public_mechanism: Create/update file contents is path-addressed; sha is required when updating an existing file; documented responses include 409 Conflict. This supports file-level CAS/conflict handling but does not provide multi-file atomicity or an effect-sink fence by itself.

shared_claim_transition.operation: unique-path create with claimant_token in content
shared_claim_transition.concurrent_result: Exactly one cooperative claimer obtains the generation claim; the other observes create conflict/existing path. After an ambiguous successful-create response, exact readback of the path distinguishes self-token success from another claimant's ownership. Duplicate delivery reuses the same logical claim path and token and therefore does not create a second generation claim.

model_protocols.permanent_monotonic_claim: Never transfer ownership after the first claim. Safe against duplicate owners, but a permanently abandoned winner stalls the work indefinitely.
model_protocols.lease_timeout_unfenced: Allow another worker to act after a wall-clock timeout without a monotonic sink/effect fencing token. A late original claimant can still commit, so timeout is not authority revocation.
model_protocols.generation_handoff_split_authority: Advance generation in a separate handoff record while terminal effect commit is guarded by a different authority object. The old effect and new handoff can both succeed in opposite objects, so a late old claimant remains a duplicate/conflict risk.
model_protocols.generation_handoff_same_authority_cas: Store {generation,status,effect_id/transition_id} in one authority file. Terminal effect commit CAS-updates that file while still at generation n/open. Handoff CAS-updates the SAME file from n/open to n+1/open. If old effect wins first, handoff conflicts or observes terminal. If handoff wins first, the old effect's stale SHA fails and re-read observes a newer generation. Claim creation for n+1 is then create-only at the new generation path. No clock-based lease is required for safety.

lease_timeout_unfenced.unsafe_condition: takeover occurred and the old claimant later resumed

generation_handoff_split_authority.unsafe_condition: handoff/effect authority split allowed a late generation-n effect after generation n+1 activation

generation_handoff_same_authority_cas.duplicate_delivery_slice: 32/32 deduped at the generation claim/terminal state
generation_handoff_same_authority_cas.rate_limit_after_claim_slice: 32/32 safety preserved; interruption does not expire ownership and a later invocation may resume or perform one fenced handoff

finding.new_narrowing: Unique-path create is sufficient for one-winner claim acquisition under a fixed destination incarnation, including ambiguous create response recovery by token readback, but it is NOT sufficient for safe takeover. Permanent claims preserve safety but lose liveness on abandonment. Timeout/lease takeover does not revoke stale authority and is unsafe without fencing. A generation handoff recorded outside the terminal effect authority has the same stale-owner hole. In this finite repository-local model, safe no-wall-clock takeover requires the generation advance and terminal effect commit to contend on the SAME current-blob-CAS authority object (or an external sink with equivalent generation fencing).
finding.important_distinction: The strong protocol does not prove that an old claimant is dead. It deliberately permits a later invocation to preempt it by advancing a monotonic generation. Safety comes from the effect-time generation fence, not from failure detection or elapsed time.
finding.repository_local_candidate: Under the fixed-destination-incarnation assumption, a create-only generation claim plus one same-file CAS authority state machine is a zero-incremental-cost, no-wall-clock-lease candidate for repository-local idempotent effects. Rate-limit interruption is fail-closed because no lease expires while the worker is unable to write.

unresolved_children.detail: The tested candidate assumes owner/name still denotes the same repository incarnation. Current tested mutation contracts lack an atomic write-time repository_id/install binding, so same-name rebind remains unresolved.

If the useful effect is outside the same CAS authority object, the external effect sink must reject stale generations or participate atomically; a separate repository handoff record alone is insufficient.

Part126 modeled ambiguous success for claim create, not ambiguous success for the generation-advance CAS or terminal-effect CAS. Those writes need transition/effect IDs and exact replay rules to avoid double-advance or duplicate terminalization after response loss.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.richer_mode_protected_manual_execution_d: none for the tested repository-local fixed-incarnation state machine; unresolved for repository-incarnation fencing and non-repository effect sinks
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.rate_limit_behavior: No same-run retry/backoff is required. A blocked mutation leaves an explicit durable claim/authority state; the next invocation may resume or make one generation-fenced handoff. Rate limiting delays progress but does not trigger a lease-expiry race.
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.quota_zero_scope_guard: This establishes absence of an added finite monthly/trial/paid compute-credit mechanism in the tested design; it is not a guarantee of continuous API availability or proof of every GitHub plan entitlement.

continuation: Part127: execute one bounded ambiguous-CAS replay model for the Part126 same-authority generation state machine under the same fixed-destination-incarnation scope. Inject response loss after a successful generation-advance CAS and after a successful terminal-effect CAS, plus a concurrent third invocation and a rate-limit interruption before readback. Require stable transition_id/effect_id, monotonic generation, current-blob CAS, and exact readback to distinguish already-applied from not-applied writes. Test whether any trace can double-advance, resurrect an old claimant, or duplicate terminal effect; keep repository-incarnation write-time fencing and non-repository sink fencing as orthogonal unresolved children.
